route_note: R1 (the project's own CMake build of csrc/: cmake -DCOMPUTE_BACKEND=cuda -DCOMPUTE_CAPABILITY=89 -S . -B build) was tried first with CUDA 13.4.92 on c38 and FAILS at configure for both commits (CMakeLists.txt is the same blob 1b9f1854 at 344e8516 and 5b28fd3f): 'CMake Error at CMakeLists.txt:82 (message): CUDA Version > 12 is not supported' (log lines: '-- CUDA Version: 134 (13.4.92)' then the error; 'Configuring incomplete, errors occurred!'). Hence the ONE alternative route R2: csrc/kernels.cu (the record's file) and the unchanged csrc/kernels.cuh and csrc/ops.cuh are copied byte-for-byte from both commits (r2_extract.sh; fixdiff.py RESULT PASS: blob sha1 equals the commit blob, diff -r buggy fixed == the fix commit's diff = 2 added lines, one __syncthreads()). The only stub is cub::Max / cub::Sum (removed in CCCL 3.0; csrc/kernels.cu calls Reduce(x, cub::Max()) / cub::Sum()), defined in r2/common/driver.cu with the CCCL 2.x definitions before the verbatim kernels.cu is #included. Everything else (cub::BlockRadixSort, BlockLoad, thrust, cublas/cusparse headers) is the CUDA 13.4 toolkit's own. Both variants use the same route and flags. CUDA 12.x toolkits exist on c38 (/usr/local/cuda-12.2, 12.5, 12.9) and would pass the CMake check, but the brief fixes the toolkit at 13.4 so that was not used.
driver: r2/common/driver.cu: launches kEstimateQuantiles<float><<<num_blocks, 512>>>(A, code, offset = 1/512, FLT_MAX, n) like csrc/ops.cu estimateQuantiles<float> (num_blocks = n/4096 rounded up; cudaMemset(code, 0, 256 floats) first), n = 16384 floats (default, argv[1] overrides) = 4 blocks x 512 threads, deterministic pseudo-normal input; the 256 estimates are compared with a host reference (per-block sort, same index arithmetic) and the number of quantiles off by more than 1e-4, the number of zero entries and a checksum of the values quantised to 1e-4 are printed.
input: 16,384 floats, 4 blocks x 512 threads, one 4096-element tile per block. Thread-level access estimate (upper bound, not measured): the SASS of kEstimateQuantiles<float> has 151 static LDS/STS/LDG/STG/ATOM instructions; assuming every one of them executes once per radix pass (8 passes for 32-bit keys with 4 bits per pass) for each of the 2048 threads gives 151 x 8 x 2048 = 2.5e6, plus the 8-trip clear loop and the 8-trip final loop (about 5e4). So at most about 2.6e6, below the 1e7 target (the record's own estimate was ~1e7).
notes: Smoke on c38 (sm_75 rebuild, not a deliverable): rc=0 for both variants, printed 'kEstimateQuantiles<float> n 16384 blocks 4 x 512 threads: quantiles differing from host reference (|d| > 1e-4): 0 of 256, zero entries 0, checksum(1e-4) 499c802cc975a09a' (identical for buggy and fixed, 30 repeated runs each: no native manifestation of the race on sm_75). The code[] values are accumulated by 4 blocks with float atomicAdd in timing-dependent order, so their low bits vary between runs; the printed checksum is taken over values quantised to 1e-4 so that stdout is stable unless a quantile is lost. Build flags (project's CMakeLists.txt): nvcc -std=c++17 --use_fast_math -rdc=true -arch=sm_89 -lineinfo (CMAKE_CUDA_FLAGS ' --use_fast_math' + -gencode, CUDA_SEPARABLE_COMPILATION ON, no CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE so no -O flag; cxx_std_14 replaced by -std=c++17, the minimum of nvcc 13). Build prints only 'ptxas warning: Value of threads per SM for entry _Z9kQuantizePfS_Phi is out of range. .minnctapersm will be ignored'. Build takes ~45 s per variant.
